scenario: A newly appointed training director at a regional opticians chain finds her team divided because half the staff uses ChatGPT while the other half uses Claude. Why should the director avoid mandating a single exclusive tool choice across the enterprise?

On a work account, check first whether it is even on: Claude turns memory on by default for individual plans, and leaves it off on Team and Enterprise until an owner enables it.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because enterprise administrators can choose to enable memory when aligned with firm policy.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because enterprise tenant memory is isolated and never transmitted to competitors.
explanation.distractor_C: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because memory is user-manageable and governed by vendor settings rather than international treaties.

subtopic: Incognito and Temporary Chats: Retention Realities

grounding: Concept 5: Memory: evolving context about you (Lines 541-543)
scenario: A corporate defense attorney uses Claude's Incognito Chat (or ChatGPT's Temporary Chat) to explore sensitive litigation settlement terms. options.A: Language models refuse to process legal questions unless all conversation turns are printed onto paper records.

The text explicitly instructs: 'Both also offer a mode that keeps a conversation out of normal history and out of memory: Claude calls it an incognito chat, ChatGPT calls it a temporary chat. Both vendors still retain a copy for a limited period, around thirty days, for safety and abuse review. So treat these modes as memory-free, not trace-free.'

subtopic: The Silent Failure of Stale Context
grounding: Concept 5: Stored context is a responsibility (Lines 555-565)
scenario: A financial controller maintains a project workspace for quarterly board reporting. Last quarter's budget model remains in the project knowledge base alongside new data. When the assistant generates this quarter's board deck, what dangerous operational failure occurs?

options.A: Stale context fails quietly: the model outputs confident, beautifully styled reports citing obsolete figures.
options.B: The cloud server crashes immediately and displays a flashing red warning banner across the executive's screen.
options.C: The spreadsheet software automatically corrupts the operating system kernel and deletes local hard drive files.
options.D: The assistant refuses to generate text and demands that the controller re-calculate all numbers by hand on paper.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option A is uniquely accurate per Section 5. Section 5 describes the silent failure of stale context: 'Stored context can hold sensitive or private information. It also goes stale, and stale context fails quietly: there is no error message, just an answer that sounds sure and is wrong. If last quarter's financial model is still in the Quarterly Board Reporting project, this quarter's board deck will quote last quarter's numbers, neatly formatted. The assistant cannot tell that what you gave it is out of date.'
explanation.distractor_A: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because stale context produces plausible text rather than system crashes or warning banners.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because obsolete project files do not corrupt operating system kernels or delete drives.
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because language models do not refuse to answer simply because reference data is outdated.

scenario: A software product designer directs Claude to generate an interactive ROI calculator widget alongside extensive user documentation. How does Claude structure this deliverable to keep the user's workspace functional?

options.A: It sends the calculator code to an external commercial print shop to be mailed as a physical booklet.
options.B: It appends the code to the user's browser bookmarks bar and immediately terminates the active session.
options.C: It opens a separate Artifact panel beside the chat, keeping the deliverable distinct from conversational scroll.
options.D: It forces the user to manually compile the calculator script inside a local command-line assembly editor.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option C is uniquely accurate per Section 6. The text defines Claude's artifact architecture: 'Chat is good for conversation. It is a poor container for finished work. If you ask for a 2,000-word report, a working calculator, a diagram, or a small application, you want the result to be a separate object, not one more message in a scroll... Claude uses artifacts. An artifact is a separate output that opens beside the conversation... You keep talking to Claude while the artifact stays there as the thing being built and revised.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because artifacts are rendered dynamically in digital format, not mailed as physical paper booklets.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because artifacts open in a dedicated UI panel and do not modify browser bookmarks or end sessions.
explanation.distractor_C: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because web-based interactive calculators render directly inside the artifact iframe preview.

grounding: Concept 6: ChatGPT: writing blocks and code blocks (Lines 598-607)
scenario: A technical writer consults an online 2024 tutorial that repeatedly instructs users to 'open Canvas' in ChatGPT to collaborate on a software manual. When she opens modern ChatGPT in late 2026, she cannot locate the Canvas button. What product interface evolution explains this change?

options.B: OpenAI completely eliminated all writing assistance features and restricted ChatGPT solely to voice calls.

options.D: Canvas was retired on current models; work is now managed in inline Writing Blocks and Code Blocks in thread.

In 2026 OpenAI retired canvas on its current models and moved the same work into the conversation itself, as writing blocks and code blocks: editable regions that sit inline in the thread. If a tutorial tells you to open canvas and you cannot find it, this is why. The design is different. The idea is identical: keep the work product separate from the discussion about the work product.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because the change was a product software design retirement, not a hardware display failure.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because ChatGPT maintains extensive text, document, and writing capabilities.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because consumer and enterprise ChatGPT features require no federal biometric clearances.

subtopic: Structured Output Discipline: Tables vs. Paragraphs
grounding: Concept 6: How to get better results (Lines 624-629)
scenario: A supply chain manager asks an AI assistant to evaluate fourteen potential packaging vendors, including pricing tiers, minimum order quantities, and delivery lead times. Why should the manager mandate structured tabular output rather than a descriptive narrative?

options.A: Narrative paragraphs consume 1,000 times more computer server electricity than structured markdown tables.
options.B: A narrative paragraph cannot be sorted, filtered, or loaded into Excel; structured tables enable analysis.
options.C: Language models are programmed to insert factual pricing hallucinations whenever writing narrative sentences.
options.D: Enterprise corporate firewalls automatically block incoming text messages that contain more than four paragraphs.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option B is uniquely accurate per Section 6. The text establishes the structured output discipline: 'If the answer is data, ask for structured output: a table or a spreadsheet file, not a paragraph. Data here means things like twelve vendors with prices and lead times, a delivery schedule, or anything a colleague will load into Excel. A paragraph about twelve vendors cannot be sorted, filtered, or pasted into a sheet. A table can.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because markdown tables and prose consume comparable compute tokens.
explanation.distractor_B: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because hallucination risk exists in all formats; tables are chosen for analytical utility and manipulation.
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because corporate firewalls inspect network packet headers, not paragraph counts in web apps.

grounding: Concept 6: How to get better results (Lines 630-631)
scenario: An executive compensation analyst requests that Claude calculate the exact total severance obligations across 450 departing employees based on an attached payroll spreadsheet. To guarantee numerical precision, how should the analyst instruct the assistant?

options.A: Demand code execution ('write and run code to get this and show it'), and inspect which column the code used.
options.B: Instruct the assistant to guess the approximate total number and round the final result up by twenty percent.
options.C: Ask the model to generate fifty paragraphs of emotional philosophical commentary regarding employee severance.
options.D: Mandate that the model convert all salary numbers into Roman numerals before performing mental arithmetic in chat.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option A is uniquely accurate per Section 6. The text instructs: 'If the answer is a number somebody will act on, ask for it computed, not written. Say "write and run code to get this, and show me the code you ran." Both assistants have a code tool for this. Anthropic counts it as a fourth home for output, beside inline chat, artifacts, and structured data, and calls the result code-executed. One limit comes with it. The run is exact, but the assistant wrote the code, and the code can still add up the wrong column, so check which column it used.'
explanation.distractor_A: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because guessing and arbitrary rounding destroys financial accuracy and auditability.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because philosophical commentary provides zero analytical value for payroll audit calculations.
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because Roman numerals lack a zero digit and severely complicate mathematical parsing.

grounding: Concept 6: How to get better results (Lines 609-623)
scenario: A hospital patient experience coordinator wants Claude to create a patient discharge checklist for new mothers. Why is prompting simply 'Build a discharge checklist' considered an ineffective prompting approach?

options.A: Because language models refuse to process requests that contain fewer than five hundred distinct prompt words.
options.B: Because short prompts cause cloud server databases to permanently lock user accounts from future web chats.
options.C: Because hospital discharge checklists are classified as classified national security secrets under defense laws.
options.D: Because specifying what it should do, who it is for, and key interactions produces functional deliverables.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option D is uniquely accurate per Section 6. The text advises: 'Do not ask for "a dashboard" or "a report." Describe what the finished thing should do... Also say who it is for. A flowchart for new employees is not the same object as a flowchart for experienced engineers. Say what format you want, too... This concept is where a lot of beginners get their first genuine surprise: you describe a useful piece of software, and working software appears.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because models readily answer brief prompts, but produce generic, unfocused outputs.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because concise prompts do not trigger server database locks or account bans.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because standard maternity discharge checklists are routine clinical guidance documents.
explanation.distractor_D: N/A (Correct Option)

scenario: A commercial property controller manages six regional shopping malls. She uploads mall lease agreements into project workspaces, and authors a dedicated standardization checklist for auditing tenant utility charge reconciliations. How are these two operational assets related?

options.A: Projects store knowledge [what]; skills perform tasks [how]. The project supplies data, the skill the method.
options.B: Projects are designed exclusively for leisure hobbies, while skills are legally mandated for commercial firms.
options.C: Skills store customer context files, while projects define reusable task execution algorithms across teams.
options.D: Projects execute code actions, while skills provide physical hardware data storage on cloud server disks.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option A is uniquely accurate per Section 7. The line to memorize is explicit: 'Projects store knowledge. Skills perform tasks. A customer-preparation skill can use the customer files stored in a project. The project supplies the what. The skill supplies the how... Instead of re-teaching the method in every chat, you package the method once.'
explanation.distractor_A: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because projects and skills are enterprise productivity frameworks used across all commercial industries.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because it exactly inverts the architectural roles of projects (context) and skills (method).
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because projects are context repositories and skills represent procedural task instructions.

scenario: A municipal IT director wants to establish standard AI operating procedures for public record redactions across both Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work without suffering proprietary vendor lock-in. Why is adopting the Agent Skills open standard advantageous?

options.A: Because the standard requires that all redaction procedures be filed with the United Nations intellectual property office.
options.B: Because skills authored under the standard are compiled into proprietary encrypted binaries readable by only one vendor.
options.C: Because skills are plain markdown folders without runtimes, allowing the same procedure to run across multiple tools.
options.D: Because the Agent Skills standard automatically grants municipal governments free, unmetered access to cloud supercomputers.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option C is uniquely accurate per Section 7. The text explains: 'Both vendors build on the Agent Skills open standard, published at agentskills.io. A skill is a folder of Markdown files with no server and no runtime behind it, which is exactly why it travels. Dozens of tools across several companies now read the same format, so a skill written for one product can be installed in another. That turns a workflow into something more durable than a prompt trapped inside one vendor.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because the open standard requires no international treaty filings or UN approvals.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because Agent Skills files are open, human-readable Markdown rather than encrypted proprietary binaries.
explanation.distractor_C: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because open packaging standards do not subsidize vendor compute infrastructure or token costs.

domain: Domain 4: Workflow Integration and Solution Design
scenario: An enterprise legal operations director installs an approved 'Contract Review Suite' in Claude Cowork. The package includes procedural audit checklists, an authenticated connector to DocuSign, specialized slash commands, and a sub-agent reviewer. What architectural composite does this package represent?

options.A: A cloud virtualization container that operates an isolated proprietary operating system on user laptops.
options.B: A plugin, which bundles skills, outside connectors, commands, and sub-agents into an installable role package.
options.C: A global standing instruction that permanently commands all cloud models to answer in legal Latin phrases.
options.D: A local device hardware driver that re-programs the physical computer graphics card to render legal fonts.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option B is uniquely accurate per Section 7. Section 7 defines plugins: 'A plugin packages capabilities for a broader kind of work. It bundles skills together with connections to outside apps, and sometimes commands and sub-agents as well, into one installable package aimed at a job function. The relationship, in one line each: a skill teaches a method; an app or connector gives access to an outside system; a plugin wraps those together.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because plugins run within the assistant's existing harness rather than deploying desktop VM containers.
explanation.distractor_B: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because plugins provide scoped tool/skill capabilities rather than imposing global Latin language rules.
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because plugins are software packages for AI assistants, not physical GPU hardware drivers.

scenario: A marketing agency operations lead compares OpenAI Custom GPTs with portable Agent Skills. She notes that while Custom GPTs provide a dedicated assistant persona with bundled instructions and knowledge, they differ from skills in one key operational dimension. What is this difference?

options.A: A Custom GPT is a standalone configured assistant, whereas a skill is a modular method that loads when tasks match.
options.B: Skills can only be written in compiled C++ code, while Custom GPTs are restricted exclusively to spoken voice commands.
options.C: Custom GPTs are legally owned by municipal governments and cannot be customized by corporate marketing agencies.
options.D: Custom GPTs automatically erase all user files from cloud storage whenever a conversation exceeds ten minutes.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option A is uniquely accurate per Section 7. The text contrasts them clearly: 'A custom GPT is a separately configured assistant that you open on purpose. It has its own instructions, persona, knowledge, and tools. That is a different thing from a skill. A short comparison: Project: stores the context for a stream of work; Skill: stores the method for doing a task; Custom GPT: gives you a separately configured assistant; Plugin: packages capabilities together.'
explanation.distractor_A: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because skills are authored in Markdown, and Custom GPTs interact through text, multimodal, and voice.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because Custom GPTs are created and owned by individual users or enterprise accounts, not municipalities.
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because Custom GPTs maintain persistent configurations and do not delete user storage files.

scenario: A research analyst at an environmental consulting firm wants to see what pre-built integrations, skills, and plugins are currently available in the Anthropic ecosystem before spending hours authoring custom integrations from scratch. subtopic: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Governance: Standard Plug vs. Trust
domain: Domain 6: Governance, Risk, and Responsible Use
grounding: Concept 8: MCP: the shared integration standard (Lines 772-780)
scenario: A technology director explains the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to his executive risk committee, describing it as 'the universal USB-C standard for connecting AI tools to enterprise systems.' What crucial caveat must the director emphasize regarding operational security?

options.A: Plugging in an MCP connector requires purchasing physical gold-plated fiber optic network cables from hardware vendors.
options.B: Enterprise firewalls automatically block all MCP traffic unless authorized by an international treaty ratified by NATO.
options.C: MCP connectors are technically incapable of connecting to enterprise services like Google Drive, Gmail, or Slack.
options.D: USB-C standardizes the physical shape, but connecting an MCP tool is a trust decision: standard plug != standard trust.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option D is uniquely accurate per Section 8. The text highlights a vital governance insight: 'The usual shorthand is USB-C for AI tools: one standard plug, so a tool built once can be used by many different assistants. Claude's custom connectors run on MCP, and ChatGPT's apps are built on it too, through the Apps SDK. That is genuinely useful, and the shorthand hides one thing you should not lose. Plugging in a USB-C cable is not a decision about trust. Connecting an MCP tool is. The plug is standard; the access is not.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because MCP is an open software protocol operating over standard digital network connections.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because MCP does not require international military alliance ratification.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because major cloud services (Drive, Slack, GitHub) are primary targets for MCP integration.
explanation.distractor_D: N/A (Correct Option)

domain: Domain 6: Governance, Risk, and Responsible Use
scenario: A financial controller considers connecting a third-party accounting analytics app to the firm's cloud AI assistant. Before granting authorization, which four systematic security and governance questions must the controller evaluate?

options.A: What can it read; can it write/send/delete/buy; do I trust the source; and am I authorized to connect this system?
options.B: What color is the app icon; how many Twitter followers does it have; who designed the logo; and is it fast?
options.C: Does the app accept credit card points; does it support dark mode; can it play audio files; and is it popular?
options.D: What is the developer's home address; what font is used in documentation; and what operating system is running?

explanation.correct_rationale: Option A is uniquely accurate per Section 8. Section 8 details the four mandatory permission checks: 'Before you connect anything, ask: 1. What can it read? 2. Can it write, send, delete, buy, or take some other action in the outside world? 3. Do I trust the source? 4. Am I allowed to connect this account or system? Treat connectors and apps the way you treat installing software: useful, and permission-gated on purpose.'
explanation.distractor_A: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because social media followers and visual branding provide zero security assurance.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because UI dark modes and audio playback capabilities are irrelevant to corporate data governance.
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because developer home addresses and font typography are superficial non-security attributes.

scenario: A corporate research strategist needs an assistant to evaluate a multi-faceted industry question: 'Compile a comprehensive 15-page market report on autonomous warehouse robotics, citing current venture funding trends, patent filings, and supplier lead times across 20 global vendors.' Which operational execution route should she select?

options.A: Web search toggle, because single-source web queries execute in under two seconds and provide brief answers.
options.B: Workplace search, because warehouse robotics venture funding disclosures are stored on the local office file server.
options.C: Standard offline chat with no tools, forcing the model to hallucinate venture funding rounds from base weights.
options.D: Research mode, because it autonomously plans an investigation, queries dozens of sources, and compiles cited reports.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option D is uniquely accurate per Section 8. The retrieval routing table maps: One current fact $\rightarrow$ Web search; Hard reasoning with no new info $\rightarrow$ Thinking mode; A thorough, cited investigation $\rightarrow$ Research mode; Internal company knowledge $\rightarrow$ Workplace search. 'Research mode is not "better search." The assistant plans an investigation, runs many searches, follows leads, reads sources, and hands back a structured report with citations. That takes minutes, not seconds. You are delegating an investigation, not asking a quick question.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because web search is designed for quick single-fact lookups, not comprehensive multi-source reports.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because internal workplace search only accesses private company files, not global robotics market data.
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because offline base models lack access to current venture funding and patent filings.
explanation.distractor_D: N/A (Correct Option)

grounding: Concept 9: Prove it on work you already know (Lines 855-906)
scenario: An academic department chair wants to evaluate whether an AI assistant can be trusted to calculate semester faculty workload distribution reports. Instead of testing the tool on live, un-graded upcoming semester data, what testing methodology should be used?

options.A: Instruct the assistant to guess faculty workloads based on alphabetical staff last name rankings in the phone book.
options.B: Execute the 5-step proving loop: test the assistant on an old completed semester whose correct answer is already known.
options.C: Delegate the entire workload distribution task to undergraduate student interns without any software assistance.
options.D: Trust the model immediately if the commercial software sales representative demonstrates a polished video demo.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option B is uniquely accurate per Section 9. Section 9 outlines the gold-standard evaluation protocol: 'The best beginner method is simple: Test the assistant on work you have already finished and already trust... The five-step proving loop: 1. Pick one recurring task. 2. Find an old example where you already know the correct result. 3. Ask the assistant to reproduce it. 4. Compare against known truth. 5. Refine and run again... Without known truth you cannot tell whether the assistant reproduced the work or just sounded like it did.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because alphabetical guessing produces arbitrary, inequitable faculty workloads.
explanation.distractor_B: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_C: Option C is incorrect because abandoning technology does not evaluate the software's capabilities or establish safe delegation.
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because vendor sales demos are the weakest form of evidence and reflect optimized marketing scenarios.

subtopic: What Proving Tests Actually Prove: Non-Transferable Accountability
domain: Domain 6: Governance, Risk, and Responsible Use
grounding: Concept 9: What does passing actually prove? (Lines 907-928, 1040-1053)
scenario: A senior municipal water district engineer runs an AI assistant through a rigorous historical proving loop on twenty past water reservoir pressure audits. The assistant reproduces past results with 100% precision. What does this passing validation prove, and what does it NOT prove?

options.A: It proves that human engineers are obsolete and authorizes the immediate termination of the municipal safety board.
options.B: It transfers all civil and criminal engineering liability to the AI vendor, relieving the engineer of oversight.
options.C: It earns tested confidence for similar future work, but never transfers professional accountability from the human engineer.
options.D: It proves the software will never experience hardware crashes, but does not prove the model understands English.

explanation.correct_rationale: Option C is uniquely accurate per Section 9. The text insists: 'What does passing actually prove? It gives you earned confidence for similar future work. It does not prove the assistant will be right on every future case. And it does not transfer responsibility. You still have to: check whether new results make sense; stand behind the final work; disclose AI assistance where that is appropriate; keep high-risk decisions under proper human control... Passing earns confidence, it never transfers accountability.'
explanation.distractor_A: Option A is incorrect because AI assists human engineers rather than eliminating safety oversight boards.
explanation.distractor_B: Option B is incorrect because legal liability never transfers to software vendors; professional engineers remain strictly answerable.
explanation.distractor_C: N/A (Correct Option)
explanation.distractor_D: Option D is incorrect because software evaluations do not guarantee server hardware uptime, and models demonstrably process English.
